fixes.was: NHS Microsoft dependency and AI security
fixes.now: AI security, governance and NHS data
fixes.reason: Names the dominant theme across the briefing's existing items in six words.

fixes.was: Siân Berry's written question on NHS reliance on Microsoft, with a matching one on the MoD's reliance on DXC, got only a cross-reference to an earlier Lords answer.
fixes.now: DHSC answered Siân Berry's question on NHS supplier dependency by referring to an earlier Lords answer; the MoD gave a substantive answer to her parallel question about DXC.
fixes.reason: 45041 received a cross-reference, but 45040 received an explanation of supplier reviews, re-procurement and transition arrangements.

fixes.was: The Lords answer HL5499 is now the Government's stated position on Microsoft dependency in the NHS
fixes.now: The DHSC answer provides only a cross-reference; the evidence does not establish what HL5499 said.
fixes.reason: The referenced answer's text is absent, so its substantive position cannot be described.

fixes.was: A consultation launched on 10 November proposes a safety certification framework for edtech
fixes.now: She said a consultation launched on 10 November proposes a safety certification framework for certain types of edtech
fixes.reason: The minister specified certain types of edtech, not all educational technology.

fixes.was: If personal data such as NHS records is accessed, the Information Commission must be told within 72 hours.
fixes.now: She said the Information Commission should be informed within 72 hours if personal data such as NHS records is accessed. Benjamin described the reporting deadline as running from awareness of a breach and the duty as covering personal data that risks harming individuals.
fixes.reason: Preserves the minister's wording and the qualifications Benjamin raised, rather than presenting an unconditional legal rule.

fixes.was: cloud computing services in scope of the Bill face a 24-hour duty to report loss-of-control incidents
fixes.now: Where an AI digital service, such as a cloud computing service, falls within the Bill's scope, she said it would have to notify regulators of significant loss-of-control incidents within 24 hours.
fixes.reason: The statement concerns proposed duties under a Bill, applies only within scope and specifies significant incidents.

fixes.was: The Bill also raises penalties.
fixes.now: She also said the Bill would increase potential penalties.
fixes.reason: The minister described an increase in the potential penalty amount, not enacted or automatically imposed penalties.

fixes.was: Lord Markham pressed for NHS data to be anonymised
fixes.now: Lord Markham pressed for NHS data to be anonymised or pseudonymised wherever possible
fixes.reason: Restores the alternatives and qualification in his question.

fixes.was: Lord Parkinson, for the Opposition
fixes.now: Lord Parkinson
fixes.reason: The supplied extract establishes his Conservative affiliation but does not explicitly identify an official Opposition speaking role.

fixes.was: Peers across parties want a firm line against a commercial text and data mining exception and in favour of transparency duties
fixes.now: Keeley called for rejection of a commercial text and data mining exception, while Knight pressed for transparency. Colville linked licensed training data to domestic AI infrastructure.
fixes.reason: The explicit rejection of an exception is Keeley's position; the extracts do not establish that all listed parties share it.

fixes.was: Lucy Rigby (Labour, Economic Secretary to the Treasury); Sam Carling (Labour); Lauren Edwards (Labour); Blake Stephenson (Conservative)
fixes.now: Lucy Rigby (Economic Secretary to the Treasury); Sam Carling; Lauren Edwards; Blake Stephenson
fixes.reason: Retains the ministerial role explicitly supplied in Hansard and removes party labels not explicitly supplied for these speakers.

fixes.was: the Senior Managers and Certification Regime (SMCR)
fixes.now: the SMCR responsibilities framework
fixes.reason: The extracts discuss SMCR and its responsibilities but do not supply its expanded name.

fixes.was: Kanishka Narayan (Labour, Minister for Artificial Intelligence); Chris McDonald (Labour, minister)
fixes.now: Kanishka Narayan (Minister for Artificial Intelligence); Chris McDonald (minister)
fixes.reason: The evidence supports their ministerial participation but does not explicitly supply these party affiliations.

fixes.was: now that the US has banned it from public use and procurement on security grounds
fixes.now: referring to what he described as an American decision to ban it from public use and procurement because of security concerns
fixes.reason: The evidence establishes Spencer's claim, not independent verification of the existence or scope of a US ban.

fixes.was: Whether energy network operators use Chinese-developed AI models (47177).
fixes.now: Whether the energy department has assessed energy network operators' use of AI models published by developers based in China (47177).
fixes.reason: 47177 asks whether an assessment has been made, not simply whether operators use such models.

fixes.was: Office of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (45810)
fixes.now: Office for Prime Minister and Cabinet (45810)
fixes.reason: Matches the office name given in answer 45810.

fixes.was: The answers also confirm that AI policy has moved to the Cabinet Office
fixes.now: The answers describe the GovAI Unit's leadership and remit, while staffing transfers remain unfinished.
fixes.reason: 34348 expressly says the transfer and reconciliation process is still being finalised.

fixes.was: What assessment has been made of civil servants using personal AI models on those devices (HL5876).
fixes.now: What assessment has been made of the use of personal AI models on government-issued devices and personal devices used to access Civil Service networks (HL5876).
fixes.reason: The question specifies device contexts, without separately identifying the users.

fixes.was: Who lobbied on the draft National Policy Statement for Data Centres?
fixes.now: Engagement on the draft National Policy Statement for Data Centres
fixes.reason: 47110 asks about entities engaged to discuss drafting. Engagement does not establish lobbying or influence.

fixes.was: The answer suggests established clusters such as the Thames Valley may come within Covenant support for grid connections.
fixes.now: The answer recognises established clusters but does not confirm their eligibility for Covenant support.
fixes.reason: The answer names no Thames Valley cluster and gives no definitive eligibility decision.

fixes.was: The answer points to a forthcoming central register or oversight of AI deployed in government
fixes.now: The answer sets out an intention to create a centralised view of deployment; it does not commit to a register or specify accountability requirements.
fixes.reason: 38703 describes an intention and the GovAI Unit's remit, not a promised register.

fixes.was: Delays to Technology Services 4 and other framework documents
fixes.now: Publication dates for Technology Services 4 and other frameworks
fixes.reason: The questions ask for reasons if documents were late; the evidence does not confirm delays.

fixes.was: the National School of Government
fixes.now: the National School of Government and Public Services
fixes.reason: Restores the organisation's full name in 46960.

fixes.was: Investigatory Powers Act
fixes.now: the Act described in his question as the 'Investigative Powers Act'
fixes.reason: 46976 uses this different wording. The corrected body reports it explicitly rather than silently substituting a statute's name.

fixes.was: Anderson tabled seven questions
fixes.now: Anderson tabled eight questions
fixes.reason: The evidence contains 47113, 47114, 47115, 47116, 47117, 47152, 47153 and 47154. The six retained bullets are labelled as examples.

fixes.was: No dedicated guidance on AI tools for domestic abuse charities
fixes.now: Guidance on AI use in domestic abuse services
fixes.reason: 42086 does not establish that dedicated guidance is absent or rule out issuing guidance.

fixes.was: Committee report: 'Innovation in the NHS: Personalised Medicine and AI – lost opportunities?'
fixes.now: Committee report: 'Innovation in the NHS: Personalised Medicine and AI–lost opportunities?'
fixes.reason: Matches the publication title supplied in the evidence.

fixes.was: the Federated Data Platform (FDP) and Palantir
fixes.now: FDP and Palantir
fixes.reason: Only the abbreviation FDP is supplied in the publication metadata; the letter's contents are absent.

fixes.was: Lisa Nandy (Labour, Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport)
fixes.now: Lisa Nandy (Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport)
fixes.reason: The statement establishes her name and role but does not explicitly supply a party affiliation.

fixes.was: Lord Doyle raised Russian cyber attacks on critical national infrastructure.
fixes.now: Lord Doyle raised Russian threats, including cyber attacks and threats to critical national infrastructure.
fixes.reason: His extract lists cyber attacks and infrastructure threats; it does not specifically describe cyber attacks on that infrastructure.

fixes.was: Blair McDougall (Labour, minister)
fixes.now: Blair McDougall
fixes.reason: The supplied contribution does not explicitly give his party or ministerial title.

fixes.was: Friday sitting from 09:30 (exact time not given)
fixes.now: Time not specified for this Bill
fixes.reason: 09:30 belongs to a different listed Bill. No time is supplied for the Artificial Superintelligence Bill.
